content: 1. Elagolix can reduce the plasma levels or therapeutic effects of dapsone by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments or close monitoring are recommended. 2. Elagolix is a weak-to-moderate inducer of CYP3A4. When co-administered with CYP3A substrates, monitor their levels closely and consider increasing their doses if necessary. 3. Elagolix decreases the levels or effects of daridorexant via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 4. Elagolix reduces the levels or effects of darifenacin through CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. 5. Elagolix increases the levels or effects of darolutamide by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters but decreases its levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are necessary. 6. Darunavir increases elagolix levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Co-administration of elagolix 200 mg BID with strong CYP3A inhibitors for more than one month is not recommended. 7. Elagolix increases the levels or effects of dasabuvir by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Elagolix decreases the levels or effects of dasatinib via CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 9. Elagolix increases the levels or effects of daunorubicin by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Elagolix reduces the levels or effects of deflazacort through CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are necessary. 11. Elagolix decreases the levels or effects of dexamethasone via CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. 12. Elagolix increases the levels or effects of dexlansoprazole by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism but decreases its levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are recommended. 13. Elagolix increases the levels or effects of diazepam by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism but decreases its levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 14. Dienogest/estradiol valerate reduces the efficacy of elagolix due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. Estrogen-containing contraceptives are expected to reduce elagolix efficacy. Nonhormonal contraceptives are recommended during and for one week after elagolix treatment. 15. Elagolix increases the levels or effects of digoxin by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Elagolix decreases the levels or effects of dihydroergotamine (oral, inhaled, or intranasal) via CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are necessary. 17. Elagolix reduces the levels or effects of diltiazem through CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. 18. Elagolix decreases the levels or effects of disopyramide via CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are required. 19. Elagolix reduces the levels or effects of docetaxel through CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 20. Elagolix decreases the levels or effects of doravirine via CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are recommended. 21. Elagolix increases the levels or effects of doxorubicin and its liposomal formulation by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters but decreases their levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 22. Elagolix reduces the levels or effects of dronabinol through CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are necessary. 23. Elagolix decreases the levels or effects of dronedarone via CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. 24. Drospirenone increases elagolix levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. 25. Elagolix increases the levels or effects of duvelisib by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters, while duvelisib increases elagolix levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are necessary. 26. Elagolix increases the levels or effects of edoxaban by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Efavirenz decreases elagolix levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, while elagolix reduces efavirenz levels. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 28. Elagolix decreases the levels or effects of elacestrant via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 29. Elagolix reduces norethindrone acetate levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are necessary. 30. Elagolix decreases the levels or effects of elbasvir/grazoprevir through CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. 31. Elagolix increases the levels or effects of eletriptan by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters but decreases its levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are required. 32. Elagolix reduces the levels or effects of eliglustat via CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 33. Elagolix decreases the levels or effects of elvitegravir via CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are recommended. 34. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases elagolix levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Co-administration of elagolix 200 mg BID with strong CYP3A inhibitors for more than one month is not recommended. 35. Enasidenib increases elagolix levels through mechanisms involving OATP1B1, OATP1B3, or BCRP substrates. Avoid co-administration unless necessary, and adjust substrate dosages as per prescribing information. 36. Encorafenib increases elagolix levels through other mechanisms, while elagolix reduces encorafenib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are necessary. 37. Enzalutamide decreases elagolix levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, while elagolix reduces enzalutamide levels. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Hormonal contraceptives are unreliable during co-administration. 38. Elagolix decreases the levels or effects of eplerenone via CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are necessary. 39. Elagolix reduces the levels or effects of ergoloid mesylates and ergotamine through CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised.
